extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing fiction writers / authors
extracted.subtask_description: A practitioner-level guide enumerating the seven essential elements of a story (theme, characters, setting, plot, conflict, point of view, style) and how to apply them to craft effective fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying lesson or message driving the narrative. Weave theme into other elements rather than stating it. Readers should discover theme through inference, not exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not lecture the reader; show theme through character choices, plot consequences, and recurring motifs. Integrate theme into scenes rather than explicitly stating it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your characters give your story the depth it needs to keep readers wanting more — they are, quite literally, the life force of your story." Personality, relationships, and motivations form the story's foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create distinct personalities, clear motivations, and meaningful relationships. Characters should drive action; avoid flat or purely functional figures. Use character goals and conflicts to generate plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: World, location, and time period. Avoid excessive description; weave exposition little by little. Setting should be felt, not described in blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal setting through sensory details, character interaction, and action rather than info-dumps. Let setting inform mood and character behavior; avoid halting pacing with long descriptive passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence of events. Critical principle: each plot point must follow from character actions using cause and effect — "this happened, therefore that happened" — not "this happened, then that happened."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure causality: events should be motivated by character decisions or prior events. Avoid random or episodic sequencing that feels like a loose 'then' chain; each plot beat should have reason and consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: "Conflict is story." The obstacles and tension driving the protagonist forward. Without conflict, no narrative pulse. Conflict tests whether the protagonist achieves their goal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal and external obstacles to raise stakes and propel scenes. Make sure conflict is present in each scene and escalates toward resolution; avoid passive or consequence-free passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrative perspective (first person, third person omniscient, third person limited, second person). Affects: - Tone of the story - Reader's sympathy with characters - What can and cannot be revealed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a POV that serves the story's needs and reader expectations; maintain consistency in POV and manage its limits (what information is accessible). Use POV to shape voice and intimacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinctive voice — pacing, tone, word choice. "No style is better than another — as long as you're being true to yourself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a consistent, honest voice that fits the story. Attend to sentence rhythm, diction, and pacing to support mood and clarity. Style choices should enhance, not distract from, story aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit evaluative criteria / success markers
rubrics_metrics.description: A story succeeds when: - Theme emerges, never lectures - Characters carry "life force" - Setting is woven, not dumped - Events follow causally (therefore, not then) - Conflict drives every scene - POV serves the story's contract with the reader - Style is consistent and honest
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these markers as a checklist for revision: remove lecturing passages, strengthen character agency, trim or integrate setting description, tighten causal links between events, ensure scene-level conflict, verify POV choices, and maintain style consistency.
